title: Sao civilisation by Lake Chad
description: Walled city-states of the Sao, remembered by their neighbours as giants, work bronze and terracotta around the lake for two millennia.

title: Empire of Kanem founded
description: The Duguwa mais rule from Njimi northeast of Lake Chad, the seed of the Kanem–Bornu empire, one of the longest-lived states in African history.

title: Kanem's rulers adopt Islam
description: Mai Hummay's new Sayfawa dynasty makes the empire a Muslim state, anchoring it in the trans-Saharan world of trade and letters.

title: Kanem lost, the court moves west
description: The Bilala drive the Sayfawa mais out of Kanem, and the empire re-centres itself in Bornu, west of the lake.

title: Ngazargamu founded
description: Mai Ali Gaji builds the empire's first permanent capital in a century, at the southern end of the Saharan trade routes.

title: Idris Alooma: Bornu at its height
description: Mai Idris Alooma, ruling for three decades with muskets and Turkish instructors, recovers Kanem and makes Bornu the strongest state in central Africa.

title: Fulani destroy Ngazargamu
description: The jihad of Usman dan Fodio burns the Bornuan capital, and the scholar al-Kanemi drives the Fulani out and takes power in fact.

title: Kukawa founded
description: The new shehu al-Kanemi builds a capital that grows into one of the great markets of central Africa.

title: Denham expedition reaches Bornu
description: Dixon Denham, Hugh Clapperton and Walter Oudney cross the Sahara from Tripoli, the first Europeans to see Lake Chad and return alive.

title: Rabih az-Zubayr conquers Bornu
description: The Sudanese warlord Rabih sacks Kukawa, kills the shehus and rules the old empire brutally from Dikwa.

title: Battle of Kousséri
description: Three French columns kill Rabih but lose Major Lamy, opening the Chad basin to French conquest.

title: Chad becomes a French colony
description: The military territory becomes a civilian colony within French Equatorial Africa, its northern half only nominally occupied.

title: Chad rallies to Free France
description: Governor Félix Éboué declares Chad for de Gaulle, the first French territory to rally, and Chadian column Leclerc marches on the Fezzan.

title: Independence from France
description: Chad becomes independent with François Tombalbaye as president.

title: FROLINAT founded
description: Northern opponents of Tombalbaye's southern-dominated rule unite in a liberation front, opening decades of civil war.

title: Libya annexes the Aouzou Strip
description: Libyan troops occupy the uranium-bearing border strip claimed from an unratified 1935 treaty, souring relations for twenty years.

title: Tombalbaye killed in a coup
description: Army officers overthrow and kill the president after years of purges and the forced 'yondo' rites, and Félix Malloum takes over.

title: Libya enters the civil war
description: 7,000 Libyan troops install Goukouni Oueddei in the capital against Hissène Habré, forcing France and the United States onto the other side.

title: Habré takes N'Djamena
description: Hissène Habré drives Goukouni out and begins a presidency whose secret police is later convicted of tens of thousands of political killings.

title: Battle of Fada
description: Chadians in Toyota pickups swarm and destroy the Libyan fortress garrison, opening the Toyota War that drives Libya out of Chad's north.

title: Déby takes power
description: Idriss Déby, a former army chief exiled in Sudan, sweeps in from Darfur, and Habré flees to Senegal.

title: Oil begins to flow
description: The Doba field starts exporting through a 1,000-kilometre pipeline to the Cameroon coast, making Chad an oil state.

title: Battle of N'Djamena
description: Rebels from the east fight into the capital and besiege Déby in his palace for three days before falling back.

title: Hissène Habré convicted
description: An African Union-backed court in Dakar convicts the former president of crimes against humanity, the first time one African state's courts try another's ruler.
